answer.rationale: memory_c2 shows switching to a low-cost vendor cuts unit cost sharply and onboarding is quick with accurate invoicing. memory_c3 shows adding a second source removes single point of failure and allocation holds through shortages. Together they support adding a second source to mitigate the 18% spend cut risk while securing lower cost, without the integration disruption of switching primary vendor (memory_c1). The incumbent refused to reopen price, and the contract expires in 14 days with line at 94% volume - adding a second source provides immediate supply continuity and leverage for price negotiation, aligns with the 18% cut mandate by reducing unit cost, and avoids delivery risk increase. Deferring decision risks shortage given no buffer; negotiating terms alone may not achieve the 18% cut if incumbent refuses. Switching primary vendor risks integration disruption and onboarding delay given tight timeline. Adding a second source is the single best use of the one sourcing decision this cycle.
